title: Elevated operator session from the terminal
summary: How the owner can be admin safely and fast from an operator agent's terminal session. Proposes a terminal-started sign-in that the owner confirms in the browser or on the phone with a passkey or authenticator code, sessions bound by proof of possession to a key that never leaves the device (TPM or Secure Enclave where present, a memory-held key otherwise), a lifetime the owner chooses at confirmation (8 hours to until revoked, 7 days by default, limited per role and binding kind) with hourly renewal by the device key without a second factor, an end after 24 hours without use and one list of elevated sessions to end any of them with one tap, named elevated action classes with rate limits instead of a stronger role, direct-action classes limited to 24 hours per arming, batch confirmation of override acceptances and archive overrides in Needs you with one tap, the testing strategy as the first route moved from Owner to a project permission, an override permission that makes approvals work, and hard refusals no token can lift. Compares owner in the browser, agent driving the owner's browser, and the elevated terminal session; recommends the elevated terminal session as the default. Seventeen decisions, threat model updates for the security Dossier, and nine slices.

implementationTasks.title: ES-3 · Terminal sign-in confirmed with step-up
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Terminal sign-in confirmed with step-up

Source: docs/operator-elevated-session/index.html (AGT-3989), extending docs/security-model/index.html (AGT-3353). Read both Dossiers and this workbench.json first, then AGENTS.md, docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html, docs/operations/security/overview.md and docs/operations/setup/operator-agent.md. Use the Dossier's recommended option for each named decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another, and record in results/status.md which option you implemented. Update docs/operations/security/overview.md and the operator agent setup guide for every behaviour you change, and append one entry to the Implementation log of the Dossier.

Dependencies: none.

Decision ES-D2 option S2, ES-D5 option A (session part).

Entry points: `backend/Features/Security/Iam/OperatorAgentEndpoints.cs` and `AccessSecurityStore.OperatorAgents.cs` (session start), `backend/Features/Security/AccessSecurityEndpoints.cs` (`/api/auth/step-up`), the access middleware, the `studio-op` CLI (see docs/operations/setup/studio-op.md), Settings > Access operator panel.

## Deliver
- Anonymous, throttled `POST` start route that takes the public key (JWK, P-256), a device label, the operator agent id and requested classes, and answers a user code (8 characters, unambiguous alphabet, 10 minutes, single use), a confirmation link, a poll handle and a 5-second interval. A poll answers pending, slow-down, denied, expired or the session.
- Confirmation page in Studio (`Confirm terminal sign-in`): shows code entry (or the code from the link with an explicit "this code is on my terminal now" tick), device label, whether the key thumbprint is known, the requesting address and whether it matches the browser's, requested classes (removable, not addable) and lifetime. Until ES-6 the lifetime choice is the existing 1 to 8 hours; ES-6 adds the long lifetimes, limits and renewal. Confirm consumes a fresh step-up; only an active Owner may confirm. Five wrong code entries per Owner in 15 minutes lock the page for 15 minutes.
- On confirmation Studio creates an `oas.*` session of the chosen agent with the device record (label, key thumbprint, address at confirmation, confirming browser session id) and returns it to the next poll. Store the key thumbprint even before ES-4 enforces it.
- Device records per operator agent: known devices, last use, `Forget device`.
- `studio-op login [--agent <name>]` runs the flow, prints code, link and a terminal QR code, writes the session to the existing `operator-session` file with mode 600, and never prints the secret.
- Revoking the confirming browser session, an Owner password reset or Owner disable ends the sessions it confirmed. Audit: `operator-signin.start`, `.confirm`, `.deny`, `.expire`, `.issue`.

## Acceptance
- A session is issued only after an Owner confirmation with a fresh second factor; without step-up the confirmation answers step-up-required.
- Expired, reused and unknown codes are refused; the sixth wrong entry within 15 minutes locks the page (tests).
- studio-op login end to end on the networked-https Playwright profile: code shown, Owner confirms in the browser, studio-op auth status reports the session; light, dark and 390 px screenshots of the confirmation page.
- The session row in Settings > Access shows device label, key thumbprint and address at confirmation.

implementationTasks.title: ES-4 · Proof-of-possession binding
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Proof-of-possession binding

Source: docs/operator-elevated-session/index.html (AGT-3989), extending docs/security-model/index.html (AGT-3353). Read both Dossiers and this workbench.json first, then AGENTS.md, docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html, docs/operations/security/overview.md and docs/operations/setup/operator-agent.md. Use the Dossier's recommended option for each named decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another, and record in results/status.md which option you implemented. Update docs/operations/security/overview.md and the operator agent setup guide for every behaviour you change, and append one entry to the Implementation log of the Dossier.

Dependencies: ES-3.

Decisions ES-D3 option B2 and ES-D4 option A (memory key).

Entry points: the access middleware (bearer resolution for `oas.*`), `studio-op`, the sign-in records from ES-3.

## Deliver
- Server: a session issued with a key thumbprint is accepted only with a `DPoP` header (RFC 9449): compact JWS with ES256, `htm`, `htu` (normalized to the public origin behind the trusted proxy), `iat` within 60 seconds, a single-use `jti` (replay cache of at least 5 minutes, bounded memory), and `ath` over the token. Optional server nonce (`DPoP-Nonce`) rotated every 5 minutes. Refusals answer 401 with `dpop-required`, `dpop-invalid`, `dpop-replayed`, `dpop-stale` or `dpop-key-mismatch` and count as refused bearer requests in the security view.
- `studio-op agent`: a resident process under the agent's OS user that generates the session key in memory at login, exposes signing over a socket with mode 600 (named pipe with a user-only ACL on Windows), and dies with the session. `studio-op` commands sign through it; the key is never written to disk.
- Two-level key preparation: the sign-in start carries the session key; ES-5 adds the hardware key certification.
- Keep unbound sessions working only when started through the old Settings path (ES-D2), shown as unbound in the session row.

## Acceptance
- A bound session's token without a proof, with a proof for another method or address, older than 60 seconds or replayed is refused in tests.
- Copying the operator-session file to another user or machine yields 401 dpop-required on every route (scripted test).
- Median added server time per request below 2 ms over 1,000 requests (measured and recorded in results).
- The memory key never appears on disk: a test searches the agent user's home and temp directories for the key material after login.

implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Hardware device keys

Source: docs/operator-elevated-session/index.html (AGT-3989), extending docs/security-model/index.html (AGT-3353). Read both Dossiers and this workbench.json first, then AGENTS.md, docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html, docs/operations/security/overview.md and docs/operations/setup/operator-agent.md. Dependencies: ES-4.

Decision ES-D3 option B2 (hardware part), ES-D4 option A.

## Deliver
- A key provider interface in `studio-op` with three implementations: Windows TPM 2.0 through the Microsoft Platform Crypto Provider (CNG, non-exportable ECDSA P-256, per user); macOS Secure Enclave (P-256, wrapped key stored in the agent user's config directory, a small signed helper if required); Linux TPM 2.0 through tpm2-tss or a PKCS#11 module. Detect availability and fall back to the memory key with a clear note.
- The device key is created once per device and agent user and signs, at login, a statement over the in-memory session key's thumbprint, the sign-in id and time. Studio verifies it against the device record's thumbprint and records binding kind `tpm`, `secure-enclave` or `memory`.
- A known device whose hardware key signature fails is treated as unknown on the confirmation page.
- Document per platform setup and the fallback in docs/operations/setup/operator-agent.md.

## Acceptance

- A copied device configuration directory on another machine does not produce a valid certification (test with a fake provider plus one recorded platform run).
- The confirmation page and the session row show the binding kind in light and dark themes.

implementationTasks.title: ES-6 · Lifetime chosen at sign-in, renewal and elevated sessions list
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Lifetime chosen at sign-in, renewal and elevated sessions list

Source: docs/operator-elevated-session/index.html (AGT-3989), extending docs/security-model/index.html (AGT-3353). Read both Dossiers and this workbench.json first, then AGENTS.md, docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html, docs/operations/security/overview.md and docs/operations/setup/operator-agent.md. Use the Dossier's recommended option for each named decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another, and record in results/status.md which option you implemented. Update docs/operations/security/overview.md and the operator agent setup guide for every behaviour you change, and append one entry to the Implementation log of the Dossier.

Dependencies: ES-4, ES-5.

Decisions ES-D5 option L2, ES-D14 option A, ES-D15 option A, ES-D17 option A. Read the section "Session lifetime" of the Dossier for the full design.

Entry points: `backend/Features/Security/Iam/AccessSecurityStore.OperatorAgents.cs` (`MaxOperatorSessionLifetime`, `OperatorSessionLifetime(int? hours)` with its 1 to 8 hour check, `RenewOperatorSession`, session validation that records `LastUsedAt`), the ES-3 sign-in records and confirmation page, the ES-4 proof check, the ES-5 key providers, `studio-op agent`, Settings > Access, `backend/Features/Security/Posture/SecurityPostureProjection.cs`.

## Deliver
- Session limits in the identity store, edited in Settings > Access > Session limits by an active Owner with a fresh step-up and written to the IAM audit: installation default lifetime (recommended 7 days), a lifetime limit per role of the confirming person (Owner: until revoked; Admin: 7 days; other roles cannot confirm), and the idle limit (24 hours, 1 hour to 7 days). An optional lifetime limit field on each operator agent. Add the session limits routes to the hard refusals so no token reaches them.
- Lifetime values: 8 hours, 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, until revoked. Effective limit = minimum of role limit, agent limit and binding-kind limit (hardware key: none extra; memory key: 24 hours; unbound Settings-path session: 8 hours). The confirmation page shows a Lifetime choice with only allowed values; it preselects the installation default, or the shorter value from `studio-op login --lifetime`; the terminal cannot preselect more than the default. The session stores the chosen end (null for until revoked) and the limits in force at confirmation.
- Renewal: the session key is certified for 60 minutes. Ten minutes before the end, `studio-op agent` generates a new session key and sends a renewal statement (session id, new key thumbprint, time) signed by the device key (hardware key from ES-5, or the memory key on memory-key hosts) together with a proof from the current key. Studio renews only if the session is live, before its chosen end and its idle end, the device is not forgotten, the confirming person is active and still has a second factor, the kill switch is off, and the current limits still admit the session's age; then it records the new thumbprint and refuses the old key. No step-up. A refusal answers a typed reason (`renewal-device-key-missing`, `session-ended`, `limit-lowered`) and `studio-op` asks for `studio-op login`. Audit `operator-session.renew` with binding kind and address.
- Idle end: the session ends when no request other than renewal arrives for the idle limit. Renewal does not update `LastUsedAt`.
- Ending events as in the Dossier's table "What ends a session": among them removal of the confirming person's last second factor, and revocation (not expiry, not sign-out) of the confirming browser session.
- Settings > Access > Elevated sessions: every live session that carries a class or runs longer than 8 hours, with operator agent, device label, binding kind, confirmed by and when, chosen lifetime and end, last use, last address, idle end, last renewal. Actions without step-up: End session, End elevation, Forget device, End all elevated sessions; effective on the next request, live connections recheck within 15 seconds. ES-7 adds the class columns. Use shared table, status and button components and the design tokens.
- Notices: a quiet notice and a row mark when a renewal comes from an address the session has not used before; a security posture notice "Elevated session running 30 days" with Keep and End, repeated 30 days after each Keep.
- `studio-op login --lifetime <8h|24h|7d|30d>`, and `studio-op auth status` shows the chosen end, idle end and binding kind.
- Remove the 8-hour cap only for bound sessions; the Settings-path bearer (S1) keeps 1 to 8 hours until ES-9.

## Acceptance
- The confirmation page offers only lifetimes up to the effective limit, preselects the installation default or the shorter value the terminal asked for, and never preselects more than the default; the chosen end is enforced (tests with a fake clock).
- Renewal signed by the device key succeeds without a second factor; it is refused for a forgotten device, a copied configuration on another machine, a disabled Owner, an engaged kill switch, a session past its end or idle end, and after a lowered limit has overtaken the session; the old session key stops working at once (tests).
- A session with only renewals and no other request for 24 hours ends; a request resets the idle clock, a renewal does not (fake clock).
- A memory-key session cannot be confirmed for more than 24 hours, an unbound session for more than 8 hours; Until revoked is offered only to the Owner on a hardware-key device (tests).
- The Elevated sessions list shows every required field and ends a session, an elevation, a device or all sessions with one tap without step-up, effective on the next request; the 30-day review and the new-address notice appear (Playwright at 1280 and 390 px, light and dark).
- Session limits change only with Owner step-up, are audited, and any token request to them is refused as a hard refusal (tests).

implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Elevated action classes and arming

Source: docs/operator-elevated-session/index.html (AGT-3989), extending docs/security-model/index.html (AGT-3353). Read both Dossiers and this workbench.json first, then AGENTS.md, docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html, docs/operations/security/overview.md and docs/operations/setup/operator-agent.md. Dependencies: ES-1, ES-2, ES-6.

Decisions ES-D6 option A, ES-D9 option A, ES-D16 option A.

## Deliver
- Session records gain `elevation`: classes, confirming Owner, uses per class and, per direct-action class, the arming start and end (24 hours from confirmation or re-arming, never past the session). Batch classes last as long as the session. The ES-3 confirmation sets the classes; `Re-arm` with step-up in the chip, the Elevated sessions list (ES-6) or on the phone starts another 24 hours for a direct-action class; the agent cannot re-arm. There is no 60-minute window any more.
- Classes in a code-owned catalogue next to the operation catalogue: `cards.accept-override` and `cards.archive-override` (mode batch, used by ES-8), `project.testing` (mode direct-action: the policy step admits `project.testing.set` without an approval while the class is armed, rate 6 per project and hour, reason required). Every change made through a direct-action class writes an operator feed entry with `Undo`, which sets the previous value back as the Owner. Adding a class is a catalogue change (T2 by construction).
- Rate limits per class persisted like grant rates; refusal `elevation-rate-exceeded`; three refusals in 10 minutes end the elevation and raise a Needs you row.
- Hard refusals stay first in the middleware: access, grants, sessions, kill switch, break-glass, secrets, production deploy and approval, catalogue, audit, `workspace.administer`. Add a test that no class can name an operation behind them.
- Header chip in the Studio shell while any session carries a class (agent, session end, remaining time of direct-action classes, End elevation, End session, link to the Elevated sessions list), using the shared status components and tokens; a quiet notice one hour before a direct-action class lapses. The Elevated sessions list (ES-6) gains the class columns: classes, uses against rate limits, remaining arming time. The kill switch ends every elevation.
- Audit entries of elevated actions carry class, reason, instruction source as stated, device thumbprint and arming id; Settings > Access > Operator activity filters them per operator agent and session.

## Acceptance
- With project.testing confirmed, an operator session sets the testing strategy without an approval; without the class or 24 hours after arming it answers approval-required; after Re-arm with step-up it works again (tests with a fake clock).
- Batch classes stay available for the whole session lifetime; the agent cannot re-arm a class (tests).
- A strategy change through the class appears in the operator feed, and Undo restores the previous strategy with an audit entry.
- The seventh change in an hour is refused with elevation-rate-exceeded; three such refusals end the elevation (tests).
- No class can admit an operation behind a hard refusal (inventory test).
- Header chip, Re-arm, End elevation and the activity filter work in Playwright at 1280 and 390 px, light and dark.

implementationTasks.title: ES-8 · Batch confirmation in Needs you
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Batch confirmation in Needs you

Source: docs/operator-elevated-session/index.html (AGT-3989), extending docs/security-model/index.html (AGT-3353). Read both Dossiers and this workbench.json first, then AGENTS.md, docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html, docs/operations/security/overview.md and docs/operations/setup/operator-agent.md. Use the Dossier's recommended option for each named decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another, and record in results/status.md which option you implemented. Update docs/operations/security/overview.md and the operator agent setup guide for every behaviour you change, and append one entry to the Implementation log of the Dossier.

Dependencies: ES-7.

Decisions ES-D9 option A, ES-D10 option A, ES-D11 option A.

## Deliver
- Route for an operator session to submit a batch: class, typed items (card, target lane, reason), instruction source; at most 25 items; lapses 30 minutes after submission. Studio checks each item: for `cards.accept-override` the card is in Human Review, its delivery is integrated and its review ran, and the item carries the review's reservation in one line; for `cards.archive-override` the card has no delivery on a protected branch. Non-qualifying items are marked and cannot be confirmed.
- Needs you class `operator-approval.pending` that counts open batches and open single approvals; its row opens a sheet usable at 390 px with one line per item (key, title, reservation, agent's reason, link), all selected by default, deselectable. One step-up (passkey or authenticator code) confirms the selected items.
- Studio executes the confirmed items in order as the operator session with `approvedBy` the Owner and the batch id, re-checking each item; an item whose card changed since submission is skipped with a reason. The agent reads the batch result; `studio-op accept --batch` and `studio-op archive --batch` submit and wait.
- The existing operator feed event and the optional push link point at the sheet.

## Acceptance
- A batch of nine acceptances is confirmed with one step-up from a 390 px viewport and all nine cards reach Completed with reason, actor and approver on each timeline (Playwright on the networked-https profile, light and dark screenshots).
- Deselected items, items whose card changed after submission and non-qualifying items are not executed and carry a reason in the result.
- Rejecting or letting a batch lapse executes nothing; a confirmed batch cannot be confirmed again.

implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Retire operator-role API tokens and flag direct edits

Source: docs/operator-elevated-session/index.html (AGT-3989), extending docs/security-model/index.html (AGT-3353). Read both Dossiers and this workbench.json first, then AGENTS.md, docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html, docs/operations/security/overview.md and docs/operations/setup/operator-agent.md. Use the Dossier's recommended option for each named decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another, and record in results/status.md which option you implemented. Update docs/operations/security/overview.md and the operator agent setup guide for every behaviour you change, and append one entry to the Implementation log of the Dossier.

Dependencies: ES-3, ES-4, ES-6, ES-8.

Decisions ES-D12 option A and ES-D13 option A.

## Deliver
- Once ES-3, ES-4 and ES-6 are live (the owner must have the long bound lifetime before the 30-day token goes): Settings > Access no longer issues API tokens with the operator role; viewer tokens stay. Existing operator-role API tokens appear as a finding in the installation security view with their holder and last use, and are refused 30 days after this slice deploys (configurable, never longer than 90 days), answering `token-kind-retired`.
- `studio-op auth status` warns when it reads an operator-role API token and names `studio-op login`.
- Settings drift: the project settings store records a content hash with every audited change; a periodic check (at most every 10 minutes) and the API start compare the file with the last audited hash and raise a security finding and a Needs you row when they differ outside an active break-glass window. The finding names the project and time, not the content.
- Update the security model's credentials table and the operator setup guide.

## Acceptance
- New operator-role API tokens are refused at creation; existing ones are listed as a finding and refused after the grace period (tests with a fake clock).
- Editing a project's settings file outside Studio raises the finding within 10 minutes; the same edit inside a break-glass window is recorded but raises no acute row (tests).
- Viewer API tokens and bound operator sessions keep working.
